text:
maya: Heads-up — since the canary of the new routing fence landed we’re seeing a class of silent socket closes for long-lived SSE clients in eu-west. Clients don’t get a close event, the stream just drops and resume fails with missing last_event_id.
jon: ack. I saw a spike around 21:09 UTC, repro from a curl -N session shows the connection gets TCP FIN without any SSE 
maya: here’s a minimal repro we used:
```
curl -v -N \\n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-3.8&resume=true'
```
sam: noticed the same pattern in the EU edge after route swap to fallback pool. The gateway sets `suppress-keepalive: true` when fence=active, which seems to let proxies close sockets quietly to reclaim capacity.
maya: console telemetry is weird: disconnect_count doesn’t increase, but client_side_reconnects and quota-retries spike. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/streaming/keepalive?orgId=1&panel=42 : the sample from ~21:08 shows the drop. obs-bot: grafana snapshot (etag: ab12cd) posted.
jon: hypothesis: when route handoff happens mid-stream we’re not flushing the last-event-id header into the resume token, so resume ends up without last_event_id and fails; proxy then tears down socket silently because `suppress-keepalive` avoids the extra ping frame.
sam: agree. Two quick mitigations: 1) flip suppress-keepalive=false behind a flag for the affected pool; 2) add an explicit `X-Stream-Flush: 1` before route swap to force an SSE comment/ping.
maya: I prefer 2) if cheap — less noisy rollback surface. But canary was trying to reduce idle sockets; we need to measure cost before reverting.
jon: also need a telemetry hook: increment `stream.handoff_flush_missing` when a resume token lacks last_event_id after a handoff. Right now console shows quota blips but no clear cause.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout paused for shard eu-west-2 at 1749813605 by @maya — reason: observed silent closes.
sam: can we add a short experiment: deploy patch that emits a single ":\n" comment before a route swap, gated by a header `X-Debug-Flush: 1` we can enable in the canary? Low-risk.
maya: SGTM. Jon can you add the metric and a quick console panel? Put the panel under Streaming -> Route Handoffs.
jon: will add metric and a one-off dashboard tile. Also adding a log line in proxy: `handoff: flushed_last_event_id=true/false` to correlate.
maya: timeline: patch + metric + canary header today. If we still see silent closes after flush, revert fence flag.
sam: FYI, observed a related client repro where client code retries with stale resume token — we should add server-side idempotency check for token timestamp and early reject with better error to avoid repeated churn.
maya: good call. Add that to the follow-up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
